races.name: Cummersdale Apprentice Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Izzari
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who rarely threatens at this level — sim-going record is thin (1W1P from 7 runs) and a return to 8f from longer trips is speculative; Cara Tuke's 7lb claim assists but the horse hasn't finished better than 6th in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Perfidia
runners_data.note: Strong prominent racer with an excellent sim-going record (13/15, 2W9P) and won over 8f on good ground recently; Tim Easterby 4/64 in 14-day window is modest but Cian Horgan's 3lb claim keeps weight competitive, and this trip and going profile suits squarely.

runners_data.name: Tees George
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent type with solid each-way form at 8f on good going — four places in his last five starts over this exact distance; Adrian Nicholls sends only 1/7 in the last 14 days but form is fresh (13 days since last run) and Oliver Carmichael's 5lb claim is useful.

runners_data.name: Hostility
runners_data.note: Confirmed front runner who sets the pace map for this race — STYLE_FIT of 0.94 flags a mild role concern on the map, but he IS the natural leader here and his last three runs show 1-2-5 form; David O'Meara sends horses in good shape and the 38-day absence is the main query.

runners_data.name: Bay Dream Believer
runners_data.note: The most compelling hold-up horse in the field with genuine wins on good ground (two wins from last five, all at 8-10f); Kyle McHugh's 5lb claim helps offset a 7-year-old's OR, and the horse's tendency to come from off the pace makes him the primary beneficiary if the race shape breaks down.

runners_data.name: Jewel Maker
runners_data.note: A 11-year-old natural hold-up horse whose form figures (074877) and sim-going record (1W1P from 7) offer little encouragement — mapped to midfield because genuine closers outnumber available rear slots, meaning his preferred ground may not materialise; STYLE_FIT 0.92 tempers expectations further.

runners_data.name: Rajawail
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up type dropped in class (OR=45) but with a 0W0P record across 13 sim-going runs and a 56-day absence — Brian Rothwell's 0/2 strike rate in 14 days gives no trainer angle to cling to; displaced from his natural rear position and unlikely to land a blow.

runners_data.name: Balance Of Trade
runners_data.note: Young three-year-old stepping back sharply in trip from marathon distances (last two runs at 16-17f) to a mile — the form doesn't translate and the horse has no wins from 14 similar-going runs; a genuine hold-up type who is mapped mid-pack rather than rear, compounding the positional challenge.

races.paceDynamic: Hostility is the sole confirmed front runner and, with no genuine pace rival to pressure her, she is expected to bowl along at a controlled, sustainable gallop from the outset on this flat Carlisle mile. Perfidia and Tees George will look to track close behind, creating a compact prominent group that is likely to set a measured rather than searching pace. The field is numerically dominated by hold-up types — Jewel Maker, Balance Of Trade, and Rajawail are all natural closers who cannot all find their preferred rear position and have been redistributed toward midfield on the map; in practice they will be further back than their mapped slots suggest, meaning the prominent horses hold a structural advantage. A controlled, single-paced gallop on good ground over a flat mile at Carlisle historically rewards those racing prominently or just off the leader rather than genuine late closers — the race shape clearly favours the handy, prominent-running profile.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hostility Controls, Prominent Win
scenarios.trigger: If Hostility leads at a fair but unchallenged tempo and the prominent horses race handily throughout.
scenarios.body: Hostility dictates terms from the front, the gallop stays honest but not frantic, and Perfidia or Tees George — both proven at the trip on good ground — pick up the pieces in the straight without needing a big kick. The prominent profile is the natural beneficiary of a race where no true pace rival forces Hostility off her rhythm.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hostility Wires The Field
scenarios.trigger: If the pace stays compressed and flat and Hostility's lead is never seriously threatened from the two-furlong pole.
scenarios.body: With no pressing rival and an apprentice claimer who rides confidently, Hostility simply stays on to win having never been headed, turning a controlled display into a wire-to-wire score. Her recent form (1-2 in last three) and OR of 65 make her the class anchor here.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Gets Lucky Break
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace quickens sharply or Hostility weakens, creating a gap for a horse finishing from midfield.
scenarios.body: Bay Dream Believer, who has the best late-run form (two wins on good ground), is the most plausible beneficiary as a genuine hold-up horse with solid recent winning form at this distance. However, because the other hold-up types (Jewel Maker, Rajawail, Balance Of Trade) are displaced rather than true positional threats, this scenario depends on something going wrong up front rather than tactical execution.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Outsider Lands
scenarios.trigger: If Hostility overcooks it or the field bunches chaotically and the race becomes a sprint home.
scenarios.body: An unlikely shape given the flat course and good ground, but if the prominent group fades collectively, a lightly-raced or fresh type from further back could steal it; Balance Of Trade dropping back to a mile from long-distance races or Rajawail on easier terms are fringe possibilities. This scenario is structurally weak given how many of the nominal hold-up horses are not truly positioned to deliver a late run.

watchPoints.text: Perfidia's sim-going record (13/15, 2W9P on Good) is the standout metric in this field — watch whether Cian Horgan can hold a handy position just behind Hostility, as that is the optimal tactical slot.
Hostility's 38-day absence is the key unknown — if she is ring-rusty she may either over-race in front or capitulate turning for home, which would dramatically change the shape of the race.

Bay Dream Believer has five wins and places from nine good-ground runs at this distance and is the most dangerous hold-up horse — watch whether Kyle McHugh can position closer than expected given the redistributed field.

The three redistributed closers — Jewel Maker, Rajawail, and Balance Of Trade — are all likely to race further back than their mapped positions suggest; if they bunch at the rear behind a slow gallop, their chance of finishing closes to near zero.

Tees George's consistency (four places from five at 8f on good) makes him a live each-way threat if Perfidia is prominent — watch how Oliver Carmichael positions him in the first furlong relative to Hostility.

races.name: National Racehorse Week 2026 EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Colin Parker Raceday 1st Nov Nursery Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Influencer Man
runners_data.note: Hold-up style suits a contested pace scenario; trainer Keatley in modest form (T14: 2/12) and the step back to 5f from 6f looks positive given the horse's best recent run came over this trip — capable of a late flourish if the front two exhaust each other.

runners_data.name: Beauty For Love
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner under Oisin Orr who will press hard for the lead from the outset; four runs on similar Good going show consistency without a win, and if she gets into a battle with Lauralynn the energy cost may prove decisive late over this sharp 5f.

runners_data.name: Onslaught
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with three consecutive placed efforts on Good ground, all over 5-6f; blinkers applied (hg:b) could sharpen early effort but style is naturally held up, and if the front-running battle is sufficiently strong this horse has the form to pick through late.

runners_data.name: Jazz Queen
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up racer whose natural style cannot be accommodated in this pace-loaded field — she will be forced to race closer than ideal, tempering her chance in a shape where the hold-up berth is already overcrowded; Hugo Palmer's string at 2/34 over 14 days is modest context.

runners_data.name: Lauralynn
runners_data.note: Front-runner with a win over this exact 5f trip and placed form over it too; 88 days off is the key question, and Declan Carroll's flat T14 strike rate (0/6) does not inspire confidence, but natural speed and course-appropriate form give her every chance of establishing the lead.

runners_data.name: Concert Pitch
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with an excellent record of placing on Good 5f ground (multiple seconds in similar conditions); Brian Ellison's T14 return of 2/16 is respectable, and this horse's profile as a consistent front-group finisher is exactly what a contested-pace scenario rewards.

runners_data.name: Excessive
runners_data.note: Prominent type fitted with a hood (hg:p) with only one placed run from three starts; step back from 6f to 5f looks appropriate but Tim Easterby's barn is firing (T14: 4/64) and this unexposed runner could outrun odds if the pace scenario creates clear daylight for prominent horses.

races.paceDynamic: Beauty For Love and Lauralynn are both confirmed front-runners and will contest the lead immediately from the gates over this sharp 5f at Carlisle, creating a genuinely contested early gallop rather than an uncontested solo lead. That friction at the front means the pace is likely to be honest-to-strong rather than dawdling, which compresses the advantage for any single pace-setter but keeps the race shape front-dominated throughout. On a flat 5f with Good ground and no real late-run opportunity, horses racing prominently in the slipstream of that duel — Concert Pitch in particular — are best placed to benefit as any leaders who have fought hard early may not quite sustain it to the line. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all find their natural position; Beauty For Love and Lauralynn are most likely to actually secure the lead, with Jazz Queen unable to get the hold-up berth that suits her best, reducing her chance in a shape that does not require that role.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Lead, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Beauty For Love and Lauralynn burn each other up early and a prominent racer swoops from just off the duel.
scenarios.body: The two front-runners fight for supremacy across the first two furlongs, setting a strong enough gallop to leave themselves vulnerable in the final 100 yards, while Concert Pitch or Onslaught — tucked just behind — pick up the pieces with a cleaner run through the race.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Lead Survives, Pace Holds
scenarios.trigger: If one front-runner establishes a small but decisive margin early and the pace is strong enough to see off all challengers.
scenarios.body: Lauralynn, with a recent win over this exact 5f trip and proven course-equivalent form, slots into a rhythm and dictates a pace that suits her stamina, while Beauty For Love fails to match strides and drops back, leaving the leader with a clean run to the line.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Splits Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early duel is fierce enough to cause significant late fade from all prominent horses and a closer delivers a late run.
scenarios.body: Influencer Man or Onslaught, racing off the pace in the rear, benefit if the front two truly burn each other out and the race falls apart, producing a late surge through spent rivals.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Closers Flood
scenarios.trigger: If the front-runners set a suicidally fast gallop and every horse off the pace gets a free passage through.
scenarios.body: This scenario depends heavily on Jazz Queen and Influencer Man finding clear runs late, but Jazz Queen in particular is not in her natural position and is unlikely to be ideally placed to capitalise even if the pace does collapse; the scenario is low probability precisely because the most prominent hold-up types are racing out of role.

watchPoints.text: Beauty For Love and Lauralynn will likely clash for the lead from the first stride — watch for either horse drifting or checking the other in the opening furlong, which could cause interference to Concert Pitch or Onslaught immediately behind.

Lauralynn returns from 88 days off and, if rustiness shows in the early strides, she may concede the lead to Beauty For Love entirely, converting this into a solo-lead race and changing the shape significantly.

Jazz Queen is effectively racing out of her preferred hold-up position and punters should note her finishing effort may be compromised if she is forced to expend energy racing closer to the pace than her form has been built on.

Onslaught wears blinkers for the first time — watch whether this draws him into the contest earlier than his natural hold-up style, which would either improve his position or cost him late if the headgear triggers an overly keen early effort.

Excessive is Tim Easterby's in-form runner (T14: 4/64) stepping back in trip with hood applied — a horse worth tracking in running to see if the prominent position is held through the middle stages, which would be a positive sign for her chance.

races.name: Christmas Community Raceday 13th Dec Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Jenever
runners_data.note: Course-fit hold-up sprinter with solid Good-ground record (sim-going 11/15), but three consecutive finishes outside the frame at 6f on Good suggest she's struggling to find the right race shape to deliver her best effort.

runners_data.name: Sixtygeesbaby
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner in the field; the STYLE_FIT flag (0.92) reflects that this is not its natural dominant position, yet with no challenger for the lead, Winn's chance to dictate is real — Good turf at Carlisle suits and 21 days since last run is fine.

runners_data.name: Stirrup Cup
runners_data.note: Classic hold-up sprinter returning after 55 days off; has shown Good-ground ability including a win on Soft/6f, but the sim-going figure (7/15) is moderate and fitness after nearly two months away is the principal question mark.

runners_data.name: Another Investment
runners_data.note: Repeatedly placed at OR=72 on Good ground in this trip (three consecutive 2nds), but the ⚠ fade flag is telling — in a pace-compressed race where the lead is not truly tested, this horse's tendency to weaken late becomes a significant liability.

runners_data.name: Maldevious
runners_data.note: Recent winner at OR=70 on Good/6f (9 days ago), wearing tp headgear, and Ben Robinson takes the ride for the strong-form Ellison yard (T14: 2/16); a natural prominent racer who is ideally placed to press Sixtygeesbaby and land a prominent-pace scenario.

runners_data.name: Great
runners_data.note: Has won twice recently (1/5f/GOO, 1/6f/GOO) and carries strong current form into this race; however, as a genuine hold-up type pushed into a midfield map position, the compressed pace scenario may leave it short of its ideal conditions — the form is there, the race shape may not be.

runners_data.name: Pickersgill
runners_data.note: Consistent performer but all five recent runs on Artificial surfaces (STA) make this Good turf appearance a going-suitability query; as a hold-up horse whose natural style cannot be expressed from a redistributed midfield berth, the tactical picture is difficult.

runners_data.name: Showtown
runners_data.note: Three-year-old prominent racer from Kevin Ryan's yard (T14: 2/31), 41 days since last run; Good-ground form limited (3/9 sim-going) and no wins in recent starts, but could press Sixtygeesbaby early enough to feature if the pace quickens.

runners_data.name: Valentine Catcher
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up type stepping down from 7-8f trips to 6f — the shorter trip may not fully suit this patient style; mapped to midfield from a true rear-rank position, and with a sim-going record of 9/15 on Good, conditions are passable but the tactical squeeze is real.

races.paceDynamic: Sixtygeesbaby is the sole confirmed front-runner in this nine-runner 6f handicap at Carlisle on Good turf, and with no genuine challenger for the lead, Mark Winn should be able to dictate a controlled, unhurried gallop from the front. That sustainable pace — essentially a slow-to-steady early tempo that quickens only late — is likely to compress the field and deny true hold-up horses the gaps they need to deliver a telling finish. Maldevious and Showtown are the likeliest horses to press from a prominent position, meaning the race develops into a straightforward front-rank contest rather than a stamina test for deep closers. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers and horses that can travel just off the pace, as the controlled tempo will reward those who are already in contention turning for home. The field contains more hold-up types than the map can place at the rear — Pickersgill, Great, and Valentine Catcher are natural hold-up horses redistributed to midfield because they are unlikely to secure their truest position in this pace scenario.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sixtygeesbaby Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Sixtygeesbaby is allowed to stride into an uncontested lead and regulate the tempo, this becomes a front-runner's race with little pressure to force a genuine test.
scenarios.body: Winn sets a measured pace, the field strings out behind him by halfway, and horses who travel prominently into the straight benefit most; the lack of a sustained gallop means closers are denied momentum.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Chase Leader Down
scenarios.trigger: If Maldevious and Showtown apply enough pressure to prevent Sixtygeesbaby from fully controlling the tempo, the early fractions quicken marginally and late-prominent runners benefit.
scenarios.body: A modestly contested race develops with a small cluster disputing the lead, and the winner emerges from that front pack in the final furlong; horses who settled just off the speed have the clearest run.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Delivers Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace somehow collapses mid-race and creates a wall of horses, a horse finding clear daylight late could pounce.
scenarios.body: Great or Jenever, if finding room on the inside of a tiring front group, might close into a place, though their redistributed map positions mean they are unlikely to be in the ideal spot to land this shape cleanly.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Wide Draw Disrupts Shape
scenarios.trigger: If horses drawn widest fail to cross early and the race fragments into multiple groups, a patient midfield mover who avoids trouble could pick up late.
scenarios.body: Stirrup Cup, returning after 55 days, or the versatile Jenever could benefit if the pace collapses unevenly, though the single confirmed pace-setter makes true fragmentation unlikely.

watchPoints.text: Sixtygeesbaby sets every pace parameter in this race — if Winn is allowed to roll along unchallenged, monitor whether the rest of the field can close the gap in the final 2f or whether the front-runner simply pockets the prize.

Maldevious's fresh win 10 days ago on the same trip and going makes it the most dangerous prominent threat to Sixtygeesbaby; watch whether Ben Robinson elects to track the leader or push up to challenge early, as that decision shapes the whole race.

Another Investment's fading pattern is a specific concern given the likely compressed, steady tempo — if the race lacks a genuine test, its habit of weakening late could cost it despite repeated placed form at this level.

Great carries the hottest recent form in the field (two wins in last four runs) but is a genuine hold-up horse operating from a compromised map position — watch for a late run that arrives too wide or too late if the pace is not honest enough.
Pickersgill's switch from All-Weather to Good turf is worth monitoring in-running; if it fails to travel with its usual rhythm, the going transition rather than pace position may be the reason.

races.name: Ladies Night 2027 On Sale Now Handicap Stakes (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Talismans Time
runners_data.note: Won over 13f on Good going and brings course-and-distance experience; Edward Bethell yard striking at 7/28 over 14 days, and 18 days fresh is within her winning range — confirmed front-runner who will lead from the outset and is the primary pace-setter to monitor throughout.

runners_data.name: Savrola
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old veteran with a win at 16f and placed form at the trip, though 45 days off and a poor recent form string (12-0-7-0) raises questions about current readiness; Dianne Sayer has 0 runners placed in 14 days, and this horse will push for the lead but may be vulnerable late.

runners_data.name: Shipshape
runners_data.note: Remarkably consistent, winning or placing in five of last six starts with two wins over 14f on Good; Bernard Llewellyn yard has had a runner placed in last 14 days, Oisin Orr is a smart tactical rider, and the prominent style suits a pace-contested race perfectly — the headgear note (hg:p) suggests he races with a hood.

runners_data.name: Dance Time
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with modest recent form (4-5-9-7-3-V) and no wins in the last 15 similar-going runs; David Loughnane yard has limited recent firepower here, and while the style suits tracking the pace, the form string gives little confidence he can convert.

runners_data.name: Ludo's Landing
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up type who rarely wins but frames the finish regularly; Jason Hart is a strong northern jockey who will ride him patiently from the rear, the headgear (hg:b) suggests blinkers for focus, and 10 days between runs is tight but Charlie Johnston's yard is in good form at 6/46 over 14 days.

runners_data.name: Gibside
runners_data.note: Has placed form over 14f on Good going and Tim Easterby's yard is live at 4/64 over 14 days; by nature a hold-up horse operating out of his preferred rearward position in this pace-heavy field, meaning his late challenge may be compromised by the number of rivals ahead of him in a strung-out race.

runners_data.name: Asia Force
runners_data.note: Three-year-old with an excellent placed record (four places in five starts), all on Good or similar ground, and K.R. Burke is a trainer who prepares hold-up horses well for longer trips; 41 days off is the main query, but the consistent form profile and Clifford Lee's patient riding make this the most credible late threat.

runners_data.name: Ouro Preto
runners_data.note: Poor recent form (7-9-7-9-0-8) with no wins or places in the last 15 similar-going runs and an OR of just 63; a natural hold-up horse who will race from further back than ideal given the field shape, with Aiden Brookes riding, and the weight of evidence strongly discounts his chance here.

races.paceDynamic: Talismans Time and Savrola are both confirmed front-runners and will contest the lead from the outset over this 1m6f trip at Carlisle, creating a genuinely contested early gallop rather than a soft, uncontested lead. Talismans Time has course form at the distance and recent winning form to press on from the front, while Savrola is the veteran pace angle who will not concede position easily, meaning the early sectionals should be honest and sustained. Shipshape and Dance Time will track prominently just off the duel, meaning the race shape compresses toward the front end with several horses competing for the same ground in the first half-mile. This race shape — a genuine two-horse pace contest over an extended trip on Good turf — consistently favours prominent racers who can sit just off the duel and pounce when the front pair tire, rather than true hold-up horses who will face a wall of traffic in a strung-out field; Gibside and Ouro Preto, both natural hold-up types, have been redistributed to midfield in the map because the field holds more genuine hold-up horses than there is space for at the rear, with Talismans Time and Savrola the horses most certain to secure their natural positions.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Duel, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Talismans Time and Savrola push each other along and the front pair tire inside the final two furlongs, allowing a prominent tracker to pick up the pieces.
scenarios.body: The contested gallop set by Talismans Time and Savrola will drain the leaders late over 1m6f on Good ground, and a horse sitting second or third throughout with a clean run will have the momentum and reserves to collar them.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Endures
scenarios.trigger: If Talismans Time dictates from the front and controls the tempo precisely enough to hold on despite Savrola's pressure.
scenarios.body: Talismans Time has recent winning form, course-and-distance familiarity in her recent runs, and Edward Bethell's yard is firing at 25% over the past 14 days; if she finds a rhythm and Savrola fades after a bold early challenge, she can last home.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If the pace burns unusually fast and the front group comes back sharply, leaving a gap for a late challenge from the rear.
scenarios.body: Asia Force is the most credible hold-up threat here, bringing strong placed form and a jockey in Clifford Lee who rides Carlisle patiently; Ludo's Landing, consistent in similar company, is also a genuine each-way possibility under Jason Hart if the race falls apart late.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Muddled Pace, Tactical Race
scenarios.trigger: If the two front-runners cancel each other out early and the pace becomes stop-start, turning this into a sprint finish.
scenarios.body: A flat Carlisle straight rewards horses who can quicken from a handy position rather than those who have been grinding from the front, but this outcome is unlikely given both confirmed pace horses have strong front-running tendencies; Shipshape and Dance Time would benefit most from a falsely-run early race that sets up a tactical finish.

watchPoints.text: Shipshape's sectional position in the first half-mile is critical — if Oisin Orr slots him directly behind the duelling pace-setters without getting squeezed out wide, he is ideally placed to strike when Talismans Time and Savrola tire.

Savrola's jumping position at the start should be noted — if the 45-day layoff leaves him sluggish early and Talismans Time escapes uncontested, the race shape shifts significantly toward Scenario B rather than a true pace duel.

Asia Force is 41 days off and stepping up noticeably in trip from 10-12f to 14f; watch for how Clifford Lee deploys him early — if he is caught too wide in the early compression of a front-loaded field, his finishing run will be compromised.

Gibside and Ouro Preto are both natural hold-up types crowded into a midfield role by the volume of pace in this race — if either makes an unexpectedly forward move early, it signals a change in race shape worth monitoring.

Dance Time's form string includes a 'V' (void/refused/unseated), which raises a behavioural flag; watch his behaviour at the stalls and in the early stages, as any erratic movement could disrupt the two front-runners immediately ahead of him.

races.name: Racing Again Wednesday 19th August Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Viviana
runners_data.note: Consistent form figure in similar Good-ground handicaps, Charlie Johnston yard in solid T14 form (6/46); races prominently, meaning she is likely to be best placed of all to track Storm Esme and challenge turning in — ideal positional profile for the dominant scenario.

runners_data.name: Douwantitrightnow
runners_data.note: Kevin Ryan runner off a 57-day break, which is a notable absence flag; genuine hold-up style and a fair record at this trip on Good ground, but he needs a stronger pace than this race is likely to supply to get competitive from behind.

runners_data.name: Sparkling Pink
runners_data.note: Adrian Nicholls horse who has won and placed multiple times on Good ground and goes in headgear; her natural closing style means she is at the rear end of a crowded hold-up group, so she will need an unusually clear passage late — style fit is materially compromised in this race shape.

runners_data.name: Storm Esme
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner, which gives her a clear tactical advantage at this distance on Good ground; she has a modest recent form string and a [STYLE_FIT] flag suggesting she is racing out of role in a lead capacity, so the key question is whether she can sustain her advantage when challenged in the final two furlongs.

runners_data.name: Leelawadee
runners_data.note: Michael Dods handler with a runner who finished second over 8f on Good ground recently, suggesting the 7f trip here may actually suit as a sharper test; genuine hold-up style and the form at similar distances makes her one of the more interesting late challengers with a real chance if positioned close enough.

runners_data.name: Only Dream Big
runners_data.note: Two wins from twelve Good-ground starts shows strong course-and-conditions suitability; wears a hood (b) and has won at both 7f and 8f, and Tim Easterby's 4/64 T14 strike rate is workmanlike — a genuine hold-up performer with solid credentials if there is enough pace to aim at.

runners_data.name: Oasis Cover
runners_data.note: Micky Hammond yard with a flat T14 record (0/5); a true hold-up type who has been placed on Good ground at shorter trips — the step up to 7f here is untested for this horse and the trainer form adds further doubt, limiting confidence despite the moderate handicap mark.

runners_data.name: Yoko
runners_data.note: David Loughnane runner who was second over 6f on Good ground and has run in headgear (h); a natural closer who needs a stronger pace than one uncontested front-runner is likely to generate — real style-fit concern, and the redistribution to midfield does not reflect the position from which she will actually race.

runners_data.name: Truly Special
runners_data.note: John Wainwright yard with a flat T14 record (0/5) and the horse returning off 64 days; a genuine hold-up type — her last win came on Soft ground at 6f, so the Good surface over 7f here represents an untested combination, and the long absence from the track is an additional risk in a competitive handicap.

races.paceDynamic: Storm Esme is the sole confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine rivals willing to press her for the lead, she is expected to bowl along at a sustainable gallop from flag to finish on Good ground over this 7f Carlisle trip. The remainder of the field is dominated by hold-up types — Yoko, Sparkling Pink, Oasis Cover and Truly Special are all natural closers who have been pushed forward on the pace map simply because the rear is overcrowded, meaning their true position in running will be further back than the map suggests. Leelawadee, Douwantitrightnow and Only Dream Big represent the primary hold-up threats from their genuine positions, while Viviana should slot in just behind Storm Esme in a prominent berth. With one horse controlling a steady, uncontested pace and a large cluster of closers all competing for the same late ground, this race shape firmly favours horses who can track the leader in second or third and quicken from a stalking position, rather than those forced to make up big gaps from the rear.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Storm Esme Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Storm Esme gets away cleanly and is allowed to control a measured pace with no rival willing to close her down in the first half.
scenarios.body: Storm Esme sets a comfortable tempo down the far side and through the turn, and any horse close enough to track her into the straight holds a decisive positional advantage; Viviana, racing prominently, is ideally placed to pounce.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Stalker Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just fast enough that Storm Esme ties up inside the final furlong, allowing a close tracker to run past.
scenarios.body: A horse sitting second or third, conserving energy behind the leader, finds a clear run and picks up the prize as the front-runner fades; this profile suits genuine hold-up types who have been racing prominently all season.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Finish Through
scenarios.trigger: If Storm Esme sets a genuinely fast early pace and the field becomes strung out, leaving late ground for the hold-up contingent.
scenarios.body: With a swift tempo draining the leaders, horses who have settled well at the back — Douwantitrightnow and Only Dream Big — have the best chance of finishing through beaten rivals; the good ground suits those who travel well and pick up cleanly in the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Muddling Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Storm Esme is checked or loses the lead early and the race degenerates into a crawl, producing a sprint finish from a bunched field.
scenarios.body: A messy, slowly-run race in which positional luck and a sharp turn of foot become the decisive factors; Yoko and Sparkling Pink, who are sharp enough to quicken from a compact group, would be the primary beneficiaries in this unlikely scenario.

watchPoints.text: Storm Esme — if she dwells at the start or is pressed sooner than expected, the entire pace dynamic collapses and the race loses its primary structure; watch whether she leads comfortably or is under pressure to do so before halfway.

Viviana — her race hinges entirely on securing the prominent tracking position behind Storm Esme; if she is slow into stride or boxed in by the hold-up cluster, her chance is materially reduced despite her suitability to the scenario.

Leelawadee — the most likely beneficiary if the front-runner tires, but she must be positioned close enough to the action given the moderate pace; watch where Mark Winn settles her in the opening furlong as it will define her chance.

Overcrowded hold-up group (Yoko, Sparkling Pink, Oasis Cover, Truly Special, Douwantitrightnow) — five horses competing for late ground behind a steady pace creates traffic risk and potential interference in the final two furlongs; congestion at the top of the home straight is probable.

Only Dream Big — Tim Easterby runs two in this race (with Storm Esme), which can occasionally lead to tactical complications; worth monitoring which horse the yard appears to be placing more faith in through market moves before the off.
